One camper was damaged as mud and rock flowed against its sides. Rainfall estimates ranged from 0.50 inches to 1.25 inches in about 30 minutes.
A spotter posted a photo on Facebook of a funnel cloud as seen looking east from Hyattville.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail in Linch.
One inch diameter hail was reported in Byron.
A trained spotter reported penny sized hail in Cowley.
Nickel sized hail was reported by a CoCoRaHs observer on the west side of Cody.
One inch diameter hail was reported about 3 miles north-northeast of Kaycee. The hail broke out windows in an antique car.
The public reported ping pong ball sized hail at the Powder River Rest Stop off of Interstate 90.
A trained spotter reported a second round of quarter sized hail north of Kaycee.

The Park County Sheriffs Office reported a weak tornado east of State Highway 120 between Cody and Meeteetse, and north of the Greybull River. The tornado was seen and photographed from several vantage points as it traveled east-northeast near the Y-U Bench.
A trained spotter reported 36 inches of snow at the High Country Lodge in the Big Horn Mountains. The Bald Mountain SNOTEL at 9380 feet elevation had an estimated 26 inches of snow.
The WYDOT sensor at Indian Creek recorded several wind gusts past 58 mph with a maximum gust of 65 mph.
A trained spotter reported nickel sized hail along the Nowood River Road northwest of Ten Sleep.
A spotter reported hail from pea to penny size a few miles north of Buffalo.
Numerous storm spotters reported pea to quarter sized hail in Jackson.
Nickel sized hail fell at the Brooks Lake Lodge.
Quarter sized hail fell in Burlington.
A trained spotter reported half dollar sized hail approximately six miles northwest of Buffalo.
A rancher reported three-quarter inch diameter hail about 15 miles southeast of Meeteetse.
Snowfall and wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph combined to create hazardous conditions across the eastern portion of Lincoln County.
A funnel cloud was observed 12 miles west of Worland.
Three-quarter inch diameter hail fell at a ranch near Sussex.
Hail up to one inch in diameter fell at a ranch 9 miles northwest of Ten Sleep.
Nickel sized hail was observed at a ranch near Sussex.
Nickel to golf ball sized hail was reported by a CoCoRaHs observer near the eastern foothills of the Bighorn Mountains. The hail fell for 10 minutes.
ASOS measured a 63 mph wind gust at Lander Hunt Field.
Outflow triggered a measured 61 mph wind gust at an automated weather sensor near the Baxter Road exit on Interstate 80.
Nickel sized hail was observed by a spotter south of Otto.
There were numerous spotter reports of hail in Greybull with the largest stones reaching the size of quarters.
A trained spotter estimated penny sized hail in Burlington.
Spotters reported penny sized hail northeast of Meeteetse.
A WYDOT weather sensor reported a 68 mph wind gust from the outflow of a thunderstorm.
A wind gust of 58 mph was measured at the Jackson Hole Mountain Resort.
The Teton County Sheriff's Office relayed that thunderstorm winds downed several trees in Wilson.
A spotter reported penny sized hail 10 miles northwest of Dubois along US Highway 26.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail.
The ASOS at the South Big Horn County Airport north of Greybull measured a wind gust of 66 mph.
One inch diameter hail was reported by a trained spotter on the west side of Dubois.
Hail up to the size of ping pong balls was reported between Burris and Crowheart.
Hail up to the size of nickels fell in Ft. Washakie.
Hail up to the size of golf balls produced vehicle damage just east of Natrona.
Ping pong ball sized hail broke windows at a residence in Powder River.
Vehicles were forced to pull over near Powder River as baseball sized hail fell from a second severe thunderstorm.
A trained spotter reported quarter sized hail near exit 210 on Interstate 25.
A funnel cloud was observed for a few minutes near Interstate 25.
A tour group at Castle Gardens was struck by hail up to 1.25 inches in diameter.
A funnel cloud was observed about 20 miles northwest of Casper.
A tornado was photographed near Cole Creek Road northeast of Evansville.

Gusty outflow wind from a collapsing rain shower blew down or broke over 100 trees at Colter Bay Campground and RV Park. Three or four of the falling trees struck and damaged vehicles at the park. One large branch, estimated to be 40 feet long and nearly one foot in diameter, struck a 30-year-old woman. The woman was life-flighted to a regional hospital with critical injuries.

A near severe thunderstorm moved south-southeast across southern Johnson County. Ranchers reported hail up to the size of nickels. Heavy rain caused minor flooding at ranches around Mayoworth. Several hay and barley fields were damaged due to the combination of hail and rain. Other damage included broken camper windows and rear-view mirrors.

Heavy rain fell in and around Barnum producing minor flash flooding. Some mud and debris was deposited by the flood on Barnum Road, which was removed by a county grading crew. Beaver Creek overflowed its banks and flooded a few ranch fields. The inundation of water caused a five foot rise in about two hours on the Middle Fork of the Powder River.
Nickel sized hail was reported near Sunshine Reservoir.
Penny to nickel sized hail was reported in Kirby.
The Hot Springs County emergency manager reported a 60 mph wind gust at Kirby.
Penny sized hail was reported at a ranch south of Barnum.
One inch diameter hail was observed by a trained spotter in Greybull.
Nickel sized hail was reported a few miles south of Wilson.
A cooperative observer near Emblem had penny sized hail at their residence.
Hail slightly larger than quarter size was photographed west of Buffalo.
Outflow from a dissipating thunderstorm produced strong and erratic outflow wind at the Rock Springs-Sweetwater County Airport. A peak gust of 75 mph was clocked at 1430MST from the southwest.
AWOS measured a peak wind gust of 59 mph at the North Big Horn County Airport.
Trained spotters reported quarter sized hail from Midwest to Edgerton.
Wind gusts of 60 mph were estimated by a trained spotter in Midwest. The wind blew down one wall of a wooden garage in town.
Trained spotters reported one inch diameter hail.
Wind gusts estimated at 60 mph broke seven-inch diameter branches from trees. A combination of the wind and quarter sized hail stripped leaves from some smaller trees.
A wind gust to 72 mph was recorded at the Jackson Hole Mountain Resort.
Wind gusts estimated at 70 mph toppled a one foot diameter aspen tree at Star Valley Ranch.
A trained spotter at Star Valley Ranch reported hail up to the size of quarters.
Nickel sized hail was seen at Moose by a trained spotter.
A public report indicated hail of penny to nickel size fell a few miles west of Jackson.
The ASOS at Big Piney-Marbleton Airport recorded an outflow thunderstorm wind gust from the northwest that measured 59 mph.
Wind gusts estimated at 70 mph were reported by a tourist at Castle Gardens.
Law enforcement reported ping pong ball sized hail in Midwest.

Heavy rain began falling around 1900MST over east Casper and the east end of Casper Mountain. Thunderstorms had approached the area from the southwest and a low-level northeast flow made for a slower progression over east Casper. The result was rainfall of one-half to one-inch in about 25 minutes. Street flooding was observed along East 2nd Street from Wyoming Boulevard toward Hat Six Road. The water was up to two feet deep near the intersection of Blackmore Road and East 2nd Street. Hail around one-half inch in diameter accumulated to a depth of several inches.||The most significant flooding occurred at the Hat Six Ranch at the east end of Casper Mountain. The steep canyons and hillsides above the ranch were torched the previous September by the Sheep Herder Hill Wildfire. Excessive rainfall quickly brought a mix of rock, mud, and debris down one canyon and another draw damaging two homes, at least three vehicles, and two all-terrain vehicles. Water and debris eventually found the Clear Fork Muddy Creek channel and spread out to be anywhere from 50 to 100 yards wide. One additional ranch received damage as the creek swept northeast and eventually topped the Hat Six Road.
Wind gusts estimated at 75 to 80 mph blew down several trees along the Bar C Ranch Road from Barnum to the Bar C Ranch.

Five large cottonwood trees were toppled and limbs up to one foot in diameter were ripped to the ground by wind gusts estimated up to 80 mph. At a ranch along West Willow Creek Road, one large feeding shed was gradually torn apart by the wind while another was rolled.

Heavy rainfall estimated by radar to be 1 to 1.5 inches in less than 30 minutes inundated areas south of Barnum and into northern Natrona County. Blue Creek was flooded as were Poker Creek and some smaller streams feeding the Middle Fork of the Powder River. Several corrals were lost and damage was done to at least one out-building. One observer said it was the worst flooding they had seen in 27 years at their residence. Bar C Gap ran 6 to 7 feet deep and Bar C Ranch Road was covered with mud and debris.||Another hard hit area centered on Willow Creek and nearby drainages along the TTT-Lone Bear Road and West Willow Creek Road. Water was running over the roads in more than one location.

Wind gusts estimated at 60 mph combined with one-half inch diameter hail to devastate barley and corn fields in northern Washakie County. There were a few cottonwood trees downed by the wind, one of which fell across State Highway 433. The same thunderstorm caused one irrigation ditch to fill quickly and produce minor flooding of a nearby road.
A trained spotter estimated wind gusts of 60 mph.
Wind gusts at a ranch near the Powder River were estimated to be 60 to 70 mph.
A collapsing shower produced a wind gust of 58 mph at the Lander Airport.
A trained spotter reported penny sized hail in Mayoworth.

A 60 mph wind gust was recorded at the Casper-Natrona County International Airport. The gust, from the northeast, was outflow from a thunderstorm east of the airport. Similar gusts tore a 3 to 4 inch diameter limb from a tree in Casper.

A landspout tornado developed near the west shoreline of Alcova Reservoir in southern Natrona County. The brief tornado was photographed from at least three different angles. The tornado remained over open land and caused no damage.

A 160-ton haystack was set ablaze by a lightning strike. The fire burned through the night but did not spread beyond the stack. The value of the 190 bales of hay that were burned was estimated at about $35,000.
The Natrona County emergency manager reported nickel sized hail along Interstate 25 near Antelope Hills north of Casper.

Thunderstorms along the south end of the Bridger Mountains produced heavy rainfall of 1.5 to 2.5 inches in about one hour. The run-off filled the Bridger Creek drainage and caused water to flood a road about 5 miles north of Lysite. The water had receded by 1945MST.
A storm chaser estimated gusts of at least 60 mph from an outflow boundary northwest of Casper.
A severe thunderstorm produced a 66 mph wind gust at Lander Hunt Field.

The public posted a picture of a tornado off of Blue Rim Road, approximately 18 miles southwest of Eden. Other public reports were received of seeing the tornado from near Seedskadee and Eden. The tornado remained over open country and caused no damage.
A 40x50 foot pole barn was ripped from its foundation and destroyed at a Missouri Valley ranch north of Riverton. Two nearby trees were toppled and blocked one lane of Paradise Valley Road.
A trained spotter 8 miles north of Daniel reported half-dollar sized hail.
A 60 mph wind gust was reported at a remote automated weather station northeast of Shell on the western slope of the Bighorn Mountains.
The public reported a downed power line down near the intersection of 8 Mile and Missouri Valley roads. A well house was also blown down.
Several reports of penny sized hail were received from the east side of Riverton.
Hail to the size of nickels was reported by a spotter in Afton.
Public reports and those of a National Weather Service employee indicated quarter sized hail south and southeast of Riverton.

Heavy rain fell in the Buffalo and Cottonwood creek drainages in northwest Natrona County along the extreme southeast slope of the Bighorn Mountains. A nearly stationary thunderstorm dropped rainfall estimated at over one to two inches in one hour. Run-off quickly reached Buffalo Creek along the Buffalo Creek Road near a rural ranch. The creek swelled to be many times its normal size and flooded the road near the ranch. Debris was left on the roadway in the wake of the flood and a five-mile stretch of the road needed repair.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms brought flooding and mudslides in, and to the south of, LaBarge. The flooding damaged 20 homes located mainly in the southwest portion of the town. Much of the flooding was confined to basements of homes and at least one church. High water scoured the channel of Birch Creek at the north end of town and exposed water and sewer pipes.||To the south of town, approximately four separate large channels along with many smaller rivulets flooded US Highway 189 between mileposts 77 and 81. The Wyoming Highway Patrol reported a mudslide near milepost 78 around Muddy Creek at 1651MST. Farther north near Names Hill another small canyon deposited mud and rock across the highway and onto private land. Five homes were damaged in the county, one of which was declared a total loss. Multiple sections of fence line were either washed away or completely buried by debris. Mud and rock plugged culverts along the highway and also buried culvert inlets. This set the stage for additional flooding across US Highway 189 over the course of the next several days.

Culverts that were plugged and buried by mud and rock from a flash flood on September 12, were unable to handle another deluge of water on the afternoon of Saturday, September 14. The heavy rain caused mudslides that covered portions of US Highway 189 south of LaBarge between mileposts 80 and 82. The road was closed at 1700MST Saturday to enable the Wyoming Department of Transportation to clean-up the debris. The road was opened the morning of September 15.
The SNOTEL site at Togwotee Pass reported 15 to 18 inches of snow.

Rain changed over to snow on the evening of September 26 and continued through the following morning. Heavy, wet snow accumulations generally ranged from 4 to 7 inches across the area. With trees still having full leaf coverage, there was widespread tree damage throughout the region with downed limbs blocking streets and causing many power outages.
The SNOTEL site at Deer Park estimated 14 inches of snow.

Rain turned to snow during the evening across the Wind River Basin and continued into the following morning. Snowfall amounts ranged from 3 inches near Shoshoni to 8 inches northwest of Riverton. The heavy, wet snow fell on trees still with full foliage and caused many limbs to break and some entire trees to fall. As a result many streets were blocked and there were widespread power outages.
The weather sensor on Chief Joseph Pass recorded several wind gusts over 75 mph, including a maximum gust of 94 mph.
Several wind gusts of over 75 mph were recorded near Clark. The strongest recorded gust was 97 mph.
Many wind gusts over 58 mph were recorded. Some of the highest were 71 mph at Fales Rock and 63 mph at Camp Creek.
A peak gust to 60 mph was recorded at Twenty Mile Hill. The Casper Airport ASOS clocked a gust of 59 mph shortly after 1200MST.
Hail up to the size of pennies covered the ground in Midwest.

A combination of hail, wind, and heavy rain caused extensive damage to crops in the Powell Valley. Most of the damage occurred to the barley crop, but beans and beets were also impacted. The storm produced one-half inch diameter hail, wind gusts to 51 mph, and nearly one-half inch of rain in less than 15 minutes.

A strong thunderstorm continued its march through northern Natrona County. The storm produced heavy rain estimated at nearly 1.5 inches in 35 minutes. The rain flooded an Interstate 25 underpass to a depth of five feet just south of Antelope Hills. Some minor flooding also occurred on northbound Interstate 25. Run-off from the heavy rain funneled toward the interstate and underpass from higher terrain to the east.
Hail up to the size of quarters was reported at a rural eastern Johnson County ranch.
Wind-driven hail up to the size of pennies caused corn crop damage west of Hyattville.
A funnel cloud was photographed just north of Interstate 80 milepost 186 near Creston Junction.
Wind gusts of 60 mph were estimated at a subdivision between Riverton and Kinnear.
Many SNOTEL stations estimated  heavy snowfall. Some amounts include 31 inches at Little Goose, 26 inches at Cloud Peak and 21 inches at Hansen Sawmill.
Very heavy snow fell at SNOTEL stations in the western Bighorn Mountains. Some of these included 27 inches at Middle Powder, 18 inches at Shell Creek and 17 inches at Powder River Pass.
Several SNOTEL sites in the Absaroka mountains reported heavy snowfall. Some totals include 27 inches at Marquette, 26 inches at Blackwater and 24 inches at Evening Star.
A trained spotter reported 6 inches of snow in Cody.
A trained spotter reported 7 inches of snow in Thermopolis.
The Owl Creek SNOTEL station reported 12 inches of snowfall.
A winter storm brought 7 inches of snow was measured at the National Weather Service office in Riverton. Total snowfall ranged from 5 inches in Pavillion to 9 inches 12 miles northeast of Lysite.
A report of 6 inches of snow in Buffalo was received on Facebook.
Interstate 25 was shut down in southern Johnson county due to strong wind and blowing snow.
Reports of 15 to 24 inches of snow were received from several SNOTEL stations; including 24 inches at the Little Warm SNOTEL.
Snowfall amounts ranged from 10 to 16 inches across the Lander Foothills.
A local television meteorologist relayed a report of 12 inches of snow near Garfield Peak. In addition, a trained spotter reported 8 inches of snow in Jeffrey City.

Most areas of Natrona County received over a foot of snow including 16.2 inches at the Casper Airport and up to 22 inches in the foothill areas of Casper Mountain. The heavy, wet snow fell on trees that still had full foliage and caused branches and in some cases whole trees to fall. Many of these landed on power lines and caused widespread power outages. Around 14,000 customers were without power at the peak of the storm.
Spotters reported 24 to 30 inches of snow on Casper Mountain.
Trained spotters reported 12 to 14 inches of snow in and around Dubois.  Up to 8 inches of snow was measured in Crowheart.
Trained spotters reported up to 8 inches of snow in Rock Springs and 4 inches in Green River.
Trained spotters reported 10 to 12 inches of snow in Wamsutter.
The Bald Mountain SNOTEL reported 12 inches of snow.
A trained spotter reported 13 inches of snow near Story. Snowfall totals on SNOTEL were around one foot west of Ft. Phil Kearny.
Wind gust to 66 mph at Camp Creek RAWS and 65 mph at Fales Rock RAWS.
KTMH 1246MST observation was 45 mph sustained. Fairly continuous sustained speeds 40mph+ from 1020-1300MST. One hour sustained criterion is the reason for 1120 start time to event.
Trained spotters reported from 6 to 9 inches across the Jackson Hole.
The WYDOT weather sensor at Tipton recorded sustained winds of up to 45 mph with a peak gust of 59 mph at 1105MST.
The weather sensor at Beaver Rim measured gusts to 61 mph over a 2.5 hour period the afternoon of December 2.
The weather sensor at the North Fork of the Popo Agie River recorded several wind gusts past 58 mph including a maximum of 64 mph.
The Two Ocean Plateau SNOTEL estimated 26 inches of snow. In addition, 22 inches of snow was estimated at the SNOTEL at Lewis Lake Divide and 14 inches at the Parker Peak SNOTEL.
The SNOTEL stations at Beartooth Lake and Evening Star estimated 19 inches of snow. 18 inches of new snow was estimated at the Blackwater SNOTEL.
The SNOTEL sites at Jackson Hole - Raymer and Grand Targhee reported 21 inches of new snow.
A wind gust to 63 mph was measured at the Clark West Sensor, DW6841.

Snow accumulations ranged from 1 to 12 inches across the Jackson Valley. The highest accumulations were reported in the northern portions of the Valley where almost 12 inches were reported west of Moran.
Numerous SNOTEL stations reported over 1 foot on snow. The maximum amount fell at the Kendall Ranger Station where 26 inches of new snow was estimated.
A trained spotter reported 8 inches of snow at the Star Valley Ranch.
A snowstorm brought widepsread 1 to 2 foot snow totals across the Salt and Wyoming Ranges. The highest amount was 30 inches that was estimated at the Blind Bull Summit SNOTEL site.
Heavy snow was reported to the north of Pinedale where over 6 inches was measured in many locations. The highest amount reported was 12.9 inches at Bondurant.
The public reported 7 inches of snow in Green River.
An estimated 6 inches of snow fell on the southwest side of Flaming Gorge Reservoir between Buckboard Marina and Burntfork.
The wind sensor 8 miles SSW of Clark recorded many wind gusts past 58 mph with a maximum of 79 mph.
There were many wind gusts past 58 mph near Clark. The maximum gusts was 74 mph 8 miles south-southwest of Clark.
The wind sensors at Clark and 8 miles SSW of Clark recorded high wind gusts. The maximum gust was 76 mph at DW6841 near Clark at 0230MST December 18.
A wind gust of 62 mph was recorded at Snow Springs Creek. A 58 mph wind gust was also recorded at the Rock Springs Airport at 2143MST December 23.
The wind sensors at Indian Creek Road and Piney Creek recorded sustained winds greater than 40 mph.
Numerous gusts past 59 mph were reported near Clark. The highest recorded gust was 89 mph.
There were numerous wind gusts past 58 mph across the Green Mountains and Rattlesnake Range. Some of the highest gusts included 79 mph at Camp Creek, 75 mph at Fales Rock and 62 mph at Beaver Rim.
Strong winds blew over a tractor trailer truck on Wyoming Boulevard to the south of Casper near McKinley street. The driver was not injured and no other vehicles were involved in the accident.
A wind gust of 65 mph was measured near Indian Creek Road. Winds gusts to 60 mph were also reported at the Buffalo airport.
Heavy snow fell over portions of the Wind River Basins. Riverton reported between 7 and 10 inches of snow with 7 inches in Hudson and 5 inches in Fort Washakie.
At the Lander airport 6.9 inches of snow was measured. Around the city of Lander amounts ranged from 6 to 8 inches.
Heavy snow in Yellowstone over 2 days. The highest amount was reported was at the Lewis Lake SNOTEL where 26 inches was reported.
Heavy snow fell over the Absaroka mountains. The highest amount recorded was 23 inches at the Evening Star SNOTEL.

Heavy snow fell across the region. Some of the highest snowfall amounts included 26 inches at the Grassy Lake SNOTEL, 24 inches at the top of the mountain at Jackson Hole and 23 inches at Grand Targhee.
Heavy snow fell across the Salt and Wyoming Ranges. Some of the highest snowfall totals included 31 inches at the Spring Creek Divide SNOTEL and 29 inches at the Willow Creek SNOTEL.
A station west of Clark recorded a wind gust to 89 mph.
A 79 mph wind gust was recorded at Red Canyon.
A wind gust of 78 mph was measured at Crowheart. In addition, a gust to 66 mph was recorded at the Dubois airport.
An 83 mph wind gust was recorded at Fales Rock; 16 miles south of Hiland. Other strong wind gusts included 77 mph at Camp Creek and 68 mph at Beaver Rim.
Numerous gusts over 58 mph were reported at Hiland including a maximum of 65 mph. The Casper International Airport reported a wind gust to 60 mph.
A 66 mph wind gust was reported at the Lander airport.
Wind gusts to 64 mph were recorded at Snow Springs RAWS. Other high wind gusts included 63 mph at Bitter Creek and 60 mph at Tipton.
A 58 mph wind gust was recorded at the Riverton Airport.
Some 59 mph wind gusts were recorded on Interstate 25 north of Kaycee.
Several wind gusts past 58 mph were recorded at the Buffalo Airport; with the maximum gust being 61 mph.
A peak wind speed of 86 mph was recorded around 1600MST at the Chief Joseph mesonet station.
Wind gusts of 82 and 83 mph were measured at Snider Basin RAWS.
A combination of high wind and blowing snow closed US Highway 16 over Powder River Pass.
A CWOP station near Powell had sustained winds above 40 mph for several hours. Another CWOP near the same location measured a gust to 62 mph.
A band of high ratio snow set up over the Cody foothills and brought heavy snow from Cody south to Meeteetse. 12 inches of snow was measured in Meeteetse and 8-12 inches around Cody.
A weather station 8 miles south of Clark measured numerous wind gusts past 58 mph including a maximum of 83 mph. Some other strong wind gusts included 67 mph at the Cody Sheriff's office.
Wind gusts of 72 mph and 60 mph were reported at the Buffalo airport.
The sensor 8 miles south-southwest of Clark measured a wind gust of 69 mph.
Numerous wind gusts over 58 mph were reported. The strongest gusts were 75 mph at Fales Rock and 68 mph at Camp Creek.
Winds were sustained over 40 mph at Hiland and Twenty Mile Hill.
The SNOTEL at Grand Targhee reported 24 inches of new snow. Some other amounts in the Tetons included 21 inches at Grassy Lake and 19 inches at Jackson Hole Mountain Resort.
The SNOTEL site at Two Oceans Plateau reported 20 inches of new snow. At Lewis Lake Divide there was 19 inches of new snow.
A trained spotter reported 12 inches of snow at Moose.
Trained spotters reported 12 inches of snow in Alpine. Bedford and Fairview each reported 10 inches of snow.
Heavy snow fell over much of the Salt and Wyoming Ranges. The Blind Bull Summit and Commissary Ridge SNOTEL sites had the most snow; with each reporting storm totals of 21 inches.
Snowfall amounts around the Upper Green River Foothills ranged from 4 to 8 inches.
The SNOTEL sites at Kendall Ranger Station and Larsen Creek each reported 13 inches of new snow.
Trained spotters reported 7 to 11 inches of snow around Cody. Around 6 inches of snow was reported in Meteteetse.
Heavy snow fell over portions of Yellowstone Park. The heaviest amounts were reported at Two Ocean Plateau and Parker Peak SNOTELS where 22 inches of new snow were reported.
Heavy snow fell in portions of the Absarokas. The highest amount was at the Blackwater SNOTEL where 22 inches of new snow was measured.

Heavy snow fell across the Teton and Gros Ventre mountains. Some of the highest amounts included 29 inches at the Granite Peak SNOTEL, 28 inches 3 miles SSW of Wilson and 26 inches at the Phillips Bench SNOTEL.
Heavy snow fell across the western Wind River Mountains. Some of the highest amounts were 30 inches at Larson Creek and 25 inches at Pocket Creek.

Very heavy snow fell over 3 days across the Salt and Wyoming Ranges. The highest amount of snow for the entire area was reported here; 46 inches at the Indian Creek SNOTEL. Other impressive amounts included 38 inches at Spring Creek and 35 inches at Blind Bull.
Heavy snow fell across the Jackson Valley. Some amounts included 14 inches at Jackson Dam and 7 to 10 inches around Moose and the town of Jackson.
Heavy snow fell throughout the Star Valley. Some of the highest amounts included 21 to 23 inches in Alpine and 14 inches on the Star Valley Ranch.
Heavy snow fell across the region. The heaviest snow was near Bondurant where 19 to 21 inches of snow was measured. Around Pinedale amounts ranged from 8 to 17 inches.
Heavy snow fell throughout southern Lincoln county. Around Cokeville 15 to 19 inches of snow was reported. A spotter in Kemmerer reported 14 inches of snow.
The Lewis Lake Divide SNOTEL site reported 26 inches of new snow.
Heavy snow fell across the region. Some of the highest amounts included 23 inches at Grand Targhee, 21 inches at Grassy Lake and 18 inches at Phillips Bench.
Trained spotters reported from 6 to 12 inches of snow across the Jackson Valley.

Over a foot of snow was reported in several locations around Alpine. 8 inches of snow was reported in Bedford. Across the lower elevations of the valley, the snow mixed with rain and held accumulations down.
Heavy snow fell across the Salt and Wyoming Ranges. The Indian Creek and Blind Bull summits both reported 22 inches of new snow.
Numerous wind gusts past 58 mph were reported at the weather sensor 5 miles WNW of Clark. The maximum gust reported was 85 mph at 0904 and 1104MST.
There were numerous wind gusts above 58 mph at across the Green and Rattlesnake Range. The maximum gusts included 77 mph at Camp Creek and 76 mph at Fales Rock.
Strong gusts were reported south of Casper. A wind gust to 69 mph was reported on Outer Drive.
Heavy snow fell in the Tetons with 15 inches reported at the Grassy Lake and Granite Creek SNOTEL sites.
Heavy snow fell across the Salt and Wyoming Ranges. The highest snowfall amounts were 17 inches reported at Indian Creek and Blind Bull Summit.
A trained spotter measured 11 inches of snow northwest of Daniel.
Numerous wind gusts past 60 mph were measured at Camp Creek. The maximum wind gust was 80 mph.
Several wind gusts over 58 mph were recorded near Clark, including a maximum of 70 mph at 2343MST on the 15th and again at 0113MST on the 16th.
Multiple wind gusts of hurricane force were recorded in the vicinity of Clark. The maximum wind gust was 5 miles WNW of Clark where a gust of 99 mph was recorded.
A wind gust of 70 mph was recorded at Beaver Rim. A gust of 66 mph was recorded at Fales Rock.
Winds were sustained between 40 and 47 mph at Hiland.
A wind gust of 75 mph was reported north of Kaycee on a sensor on Interstate 25.
Numerous wind gusts past 90 mph were reported near Clark including a maximum gust of 104 mph.
A winds gust to 59 mph was reported at Camp Creek.
Winds were sustained above 40 mph for several hours at Hiland. A mesonet station in southwest Casper recorded a peak gust of 60 mph at 1242MST.
Winds of 20 to 30 mph with occasional gusts to 35 mph combined with at least 5 inches of snowfall to create difficult travel conditions on I-80 in eastern Sweetwater County.
Winds of 20 to 30 mph combined with snowfall of 5 to 6 inches to create winter storm conditions around Kemmerer.
Heavy snow fell in the Cody foothills. Amounts generally ranged from 6 to 8 inches from Cody southward to Meeteetse.
Snowfall at the south end of Star Valley generally ranged from 6 to 12 inches.
Over a foot of snow was reported at the Two Ocean and Lewis Lake Divide SNOTELS. The snow continued into March.
Over two feet of snow fell by the end of the month at the Grand Targhee and Grassy Lake SNOTELS. The storm continued into March as well.
Trained spotters reported 7 inches of snow was reported near Moose by sunrise on the 28th. The storm continued into March.
Snow began to accumulate in the higher elevations of the zone on February 27. The snow continued into February.
Heavy snow began falling on the 28th. The snow continued into March when the heaviest snow fell.
Heavy snow began falling on the evening of the 28th. The heaviest snow fell in March.
Heavy snow fell in the Absarokas. 12 inches of snow fell at Evening Star by the end of February 28. The snow continued into March.
Snow began falling in the western Bighorn range in the early morning of February 28. The snow continued into March 1.
Heavy snow began falling on the evening of February 28th. Snow continued into March 1st.
Snow began falling in Natrona county on the morning of the 28th. Snow continued into March 1.
Heavy snow continued to fall in Yellowstone Park. The highest storm totals included 27 inches at the Snake River Ranger Station and 21 inches at the Yellowstone East Entrance.

Very heavy snow continued into March from February. The area around the Grand Targhee ski resort at the most snow with 38 inches recorded at the SNOTEL with 34 inches measured at the ski area. The areas near the Jackson Hole ski area were also hard hit with over 2 feet commonplace.

Heavy snow fell across the Jackson Valley. The northern Jackson Valley had the most with Moose receiving anywhere from 20 to 24 inches. There were lesser amounts toward Jackson where amounts around a foot were commonplace.
Heavy snow fell across the Salt and Wyoming Range. The highest amounts were 23 inches at Indian Creek and 20 inches at Blind Bull summit.
The public and a COOP observer totaled 16-17 of snow in Bondurant.
Heavy snow fell across the western slopes of the Wind River Range. Some of the highest amounts included 26 inches at the Kendall Ranger Station and 18 inches at Larson Creek.
Heavy snow continued across the eastern slopes of the Wind River Range. The highest amounts included 18 inches at the South Pass SNOTEL and 14.5 inches in Atlantic City.
Heavy snow continued into the first of March. The highest amounts included 20 inches at Blackwater and 19 inches at Evening Star.
The SNOTEL at Bone Spring recorded 12 inches of new snow.
The trained spotter reported 6 inches of snow at Jeffrey City.
Snow continued from the previous day. The Casper COOP observer reported a storm total of 8.2 inches. Reports of 6 to 7 inches were common around the south side of Casper.
Consistent wind gusts above 60 mph and in many cases 70 mph were recorded at a sensor 5 miles west-northwest of Clark. The maximum wind gust was 80 mph.
There were several gusts over 58 mph at Fales Rock, including a maximum of 62 mph.
A 60 mph wind gust was measured at Outer Drive south of Casper.
A 61 mph wind gust was recorded at Fales Rock.
Wind gusts to 58 mph were recorded on Outer Drive near Casper.
Strong wind gusts were measured at Camp Creek and Fales Rock, with gusts to 62 and 60 mph, respectively.
Winds were sustained at over 40 mph at the Casper/Natrona County International Airport.

The ASOS at the Rock Springs airport recorded a wind gusts of 59 mph. Other peak gusts in the area included 63 mph at Snow Springs and 60 mph at Bitter Creek. The mesonet site at Bitter Creek also recorded several hours of sustained wind exceeding 40 mph.
The WYDOT sensor at Piney Creek on Interstate 90 registered sustained winds of 40 mph.
Winds were measured at 51 mph sustained with gusts to 63 mph at the WYDOT sensor on Interstate 25 north of Kaycee along Reno Hill.
The ASOS at the South Big Horn County Airport north of Greybull recorded a wind gust of 64 mph.
A wind sensor 5 miles west-northwest of Clark recorded several wind gusts of hurricane force, including a maximum gust of 110 mph at 0926MST.
A second wind event occurred in the Cody Foothills. Winds were sustained at 50 mph with gusts to 70 mph at a sensor on US 120 north of Meeteetse.
Camp Creek RAWS recorded a 69 mph gust while Fales Rock RAWS topped out at 61 mph.
The Clark 8SSW sensor on State Highway 120 clocked a 65 mph gust. Two gusts to 58 mph were recorded at a station west of Clark.
Wind gusts to 78 mph and 91 mph were registered at stations 8 miles SSW and just west of Clark, respectively.
A 59 mph wind gust was reported at the Johnson County Airport ASOS in Buffalo.
A 59 mph wind gust was recorded at the Lander Airport. A gust to 63 mph was reported 7 miles NW of Lander.
The Chief Joseph mesonet site topped out at 89 mph just before 1330MST.

Heavy snow fell in Yellowstone National Park. The highest amount recorded was at the Thumb Divide SNOTEL where 22 inches was recorded. Some other amounts included 19 inches at Parker Peak and 18 inches at Lewis Lake.

Heavy snow fell across portions of the Tetons. The highest amount recorded was 19 inches at the Grassy Lake SNOTEL. Other amounts included 18 inches at Jackson Hole Mountain Resort and 17 inches at Grand Targhee.

The weather sensor at Chief Joseph measured several wind gusts of hurricane force, including a maximum gust of 79 mph. Sustained speeds were commonly in excess of 50 mph with a peak of 59 mph at 1045MST.

The wind sensor 5 miles west-northwest of Clark recorded many wind gusts past 74 mph, including a maximum of 89 mph. In addition, a wind gust of 59 mph and more than one hour of 40+ mph sustained wind were recorded north of Meeteetse along Highway 120.
The weather sensor at Fales Rock recorded a wind gust of 68 mph.
The weather sensor on Outer Drive south of Casper recorded a wind gust of 51 knots.
Snowfall of 9-10 inches fell at Bondurant with only 2-3 inches in Pinedale.
Snowfall totals around Dubois ranged from 6 to 10 inches.
The public and a COOP observer totaled 16-17 of snow in Bondurant.
A trained spotter reported 7 inches of snow in Meeteetsee.
A NWS employee measured 6 inches of snow in Lander.
Six inches of snow fell on the south side of Casper.
Mesoscale convective banding produced locally heavy snowfall in the northern Big Horn Basin. At Greybull 11 inches of snow fell with 9 inches reported at Otto.
A spotter 9.5 miles SW of Lander measured 16 inches of snow.
Snowfall of 12 to 15 inches was measured on Casper Mountain.
The ASOS at Riverton Regional Airport measured a wind gust of 61 mph at 1924MST.
The ASOS at Hunt Field in Lander registered a wind gust of 61 mph. A mesonet sensor in the Lander Foothills on the North Fork of the Popo Agie River measured multiple gusts of 59 mph.
Several wind gusts past 58 mph were recorded 5 miles WNW of Clark including a maximum of 76 mph. In addition, a gust to 58 mph was recorded at Meeteetse.
Winds were sustained over 40 mph for almost 2 hours at Red Canyon with a maximum gust of 60 mph.
A wind gust to 68 mph was measured at the Big Piney Airport.
Numerous wind gusts past 58 mph were reported on State Highway 120 north of Meeteetse, including a maximum of 73 mph.
A 62 mph wind gust was recorded at the airport near Greybull.
A trained spotter sighted a weak tornado north of Missouri Valley Road. The tornado remained over open country and caused no damage.
Hail to the size of pennies was observed at Boysen State Park.
A trained spotter estimated half dollar sized hail in Midwest. In addition, hail the size of nickels fell in Edgerton.

Ice jam flooding caused damage in Worland. Neighborhoods near the river north and south of the Highway 789 bridge reported flooding of some homes. The water extended 100-200 yards from the river's edge at a depth of 12 to 18 inches.

An ice jam caused flooding around the town of Manderson near the confluence of the Big Horn and Nowood rivers. The National Guard was called in to assist with sandbagging and other protective measures on March 9 and 10.
A mesonet sensor at Seedskadee National Wildlife Refuge recorded wind gusts to 59 mph with sustained speeds as high as 43 mph.
A tornado was observed near Sand Mesa Road in northern Fremont County. Several power poles were toppled as the tornado traveled northeast toward a rural ranch before dissipating.

Flooding of two ranches occurred along the Nowood River north of Ten Sleep. The ice jams formed on several bends in the serpentine river flooding ranch lands. At least one resident evacuated their residence as the water level climbed.
Flooding of the Spence Oil Field and other areas north of Greybull occurred along the Big Horn River. Three homes outside the Greybull levee system had minor flooding.
A tornado on the southwest side of Casper Mountain in the vicinity of Jackson Canyon was seen and photographed by people from across Casper.

A trained spotter observed a landspout tornado for several minutes near the North Big Horn County Airport north of Cowley. The tornado was nearly stationary for a few minutes and moved slowly to the southeast and nearly crossed the airport runway.

A 31-year-old man was injured when lightning struck him on the practice putting green at White Mountain Golf Course on the north side of Rock Springs. A witness to the incident was able to revive the man with CPR and a defibrillator.
Snowfall of 6 to 10 inches fell along Beaver Rim.
High winds blew for most of the day across northern Johnson County. Wind gusts exceeded 60 mph with a peak of 70 mph.
One inch diameter hail was reported at a ranch along Sand Mesa Road.
Trained spotters measured 20 to 23 inches of new snow on Casper Mountain.
The cooperative observer at Jeffrey City reported 9 inches of snow.
A trained spotter measured 6 inches of snow in Wamsutter.
Heavy snow fell across the eastern slopes of the Wind River Range. Some the higher amounts included 22 inches at Townsend Creek, 19 inches at Hobbs Park and 18 inches at Hobbs Park.

Heavy thunderstorm rains of four to six inches fell to the east over Campbell County and along the Johnson-Campbell County line filling the Dead Horse Creek drainage with heavy run-off. The resultant high water caused flash flooding of Dead Horse Creek near milepost 90 on Interstate 90 in eastern Johnson County. The flooding caused the shutdown of the interstate between Buffalo and Gillette for about four hours between 2100 MST on Saturday, May 24, and 0100MST on Sunday, May 25.
Shingles were blown off the roof of a ranch house north of Ten Sleep.
A wind gust to 62 mph was recorded at a ranch on the North Fork of the Popo Agie River west of Milford.
The ASOS at the Worland Airport reported a wind gust of 65 mph from a weak shower sweeping northeast.
A wind gust of 58 mph was recorded at the Johnson County Airport in Buffalo. Weak convection lacking any lightning was responsible for the wind gust.

A large roof section was torn from a home in the small community of Reliance north of Rock Springs. Strong wind also toppled a utility pole and did damage to a nearby fence. Weak convection was responsible for the wind gust, as there was no thunderstorm in the area.
Several power poles were reported down west-northwest of Green River toward State Highway 372. The wind gusts were associated with weak convection and not a thunderstorm.
Hail to the size of pennies was reported in Worland.
Numerous spotters reported nickel to quarter sized hail in and around Colter Bay.
Hail the size of quarters was reported in Lovell.
A tornado touched down briefly on Dollar Lake. The tornado sucked up water from the lake before lifting. No damage was reported.

An off-duty NWS meteorologist reported hail up to the size of pennies covering US 20/26 around Waltman and Hells Half Acre. The hail fell for about 15 minutes and covered the highway to a depth of two inches.
A rancher north of Anchor Reservoir observed a brief tornado near Putney Flat in the Owl Creek drainage. The tornado remained over open country and did no damage.
Worland Fire Department personnel reported a funnel cloud in Hot Springs County that was about three-quarters of the way to the ground.
The ASOS at Hunt Field in Lander measured a wind gust of 63 mph.
Nickel sized hail was reported just west of Kaycee and Interstate 25.
Nickel sized hail was reported at a ranch along Sand Draw Road.
The ASOS at the Casper-Natrona County International Airport reported a peak wind gust of 59 mph.
Numerous trained spotters reported penny to nickel sized hail in and around Riverton.
The public reported nickel sized hail on the west side of Cody.
An off-duty NWS employee reported penny sized hail along Missouri Valley Road.
Penny sized hail was observed in Fort Washakie.
Hail up to one inch in diameter was measured at Castle Gardens. The hail lasted for approximately 15 minutes and accumulated to a depth of two inches.
A COOP observer reported nickel sized hail in Hudson.

An off-duty NWS employee reported 0.75 inch diameter hail. In addition, rainfall of around one-half inch to about one inch fell in less than 30 minutes. The result was minor street flooding in many areas of central and east Riverton.
An anemometer at the NWS office northwest of Riverton registered a wind gust to 65 mph.
The ASOS at Riverton Regional Airport measured a peak wind gust of 62 mph.
A 67 mph wind gust was measured by a mesonet sensor near Indian Creek Road on Interstate 90.
A peak wind of 60 mph was measured by the ASOS at the South Big Horn County Airport north of Greybull.
Penny sized hail fell at a residence near the Riverton Country Club.
The peak wind reached 60 mph on the ASOS at Lander Hunt Field. The wind was associated with weak convection.

Microburst winds caused damage in a broad area of central Rock Springs just prior to 2200MST. Siding was torn from the side of one home, another had an exterior door and window broken, and there were numerous reports of broken tree limbs.
Nickel sized hail was observed on the north side of Lovell.
An off-duty US Forest Service employee photographed a funnel cloud northwest of Green River Lakes.
Hail up to one inch in diameter was observed at a ranch east of Kaycee.

Golf ball sized and larger hail fell at a ranch east of Kaycee along State Highway 192. The largest stones were 3 inches in diameter. The large hail broke windows and screens, cracked a few windshields, and caused minor damage to ranch buildings.
The community of Winchester was hit with three to four minutes of nickel to quarter sized hail.

A prolonged period of penny to nickel sized hail fell along Interstate 90 near the Powder River. The hail covered the interstate to a depth of five to six inches and reduced traffic to a single lane in some spots. The combination of rain and hail caused minor flooding on Dry Creek along the Powder River Road about three miles north of the interstate.
The ASOS at the Big Piney Airport clocked a peak wind gust of 60 mph shortly before 1900MST.

Lightning struck near the 3rd green at the Powell Golf Club near Garland. The strike affected four golfers, one of which was knocked to the ground. The hole they were finishing was on an elevated portion of the course at the far north end of the property.

A weak tornado was photographed south of Eden just to the west of US Highway 191. No damage was reported and the tornado did not cross the highway. At least one other reporting party witnessed the tornado.

Melting snow produced minor flooding on the Wind River near Dubois. The river hit flood stage of 5.0 feet at 0445MST on Wednesday, May 28, and remained near that mark through the end of the month. The peak stage was 5.32 feet at 0415MST on Friday, May 30. The diurnal snowmelt pattern generated the highest water levels between 0100 and 0400MST each day. Damage to buildings and infrastructure did not occur.

Water from melting snow traveled down the main stem of the Wind River to Riverton and produced minor flooding. The river gauge at Riverton climbed above flood stage of 9.0 feet late on Wednesday, May 28. The river hovered around or just above flood stage through the end of the month. The peak stage was 9.52 feet between 0415 and 0430MST on May 31. The flooding only impacted lowland areas nearest the river.

Flood stage of 3.5 feet on Medicine Lodge Creek within the boundaries of Medicine Lodge State Archaeological Site was topped beginning at 0300MST on Thursday, May 29. The water level generally stayed above flood stage through the end of the month. The creek crested at 4.07 feet at 0115MST on May 30, and nearly repeated the same feat the following morning reaching 4.06 feet. Peak water levels occurred between 0115 and 0345MST each day. State park employees sandbagged the creek and successfully protected the main road through the archaeological site. Some minor flooding of a few campsites did occur.
Thunderstorm outflow toppled two large trees at Medicine Lodge State Archaeological Site. The falling trees damaged a fence and narrowly missed a small cabin on the property.

Minor flooding on the Wind River near Dubois came to an end at 0600MST on Sunday, June 1, as the river receded below flood stage of 5.0 feet. Cooler air sweeping across Wyoming along with a decreasing snowpack slowed the snowmelt and ended the flood threat for the season. Sandbagging was completed for a few homes with riverfront property to protect them from flood waters.

Cooler air behind a cold front and a decreasing mountain snowpack helped the Wind River recede to below flood stage of 9.0 feet at 0645MST on Sunday, June 1. The only areas impacted by the flood waters were lowlands nearest the river.

The gauge on Medicine Lodge Creek in Medicine Lodge State Archaeological Site fell below flood stage of 3.5 feet at 0915MST on Sunday, June 1. A decreasing mountain snowpack and cooler air in the wake of a cold front brought an end to the snowmelt and flooding. The river ran high for roughly the first half of June but additional flooding did not occur.

A rapidly developing thunderstorm produced a funnel cloud near the Casper-Natrona County International Airport. The funnel dissipated and reformed several times. Many people, including the county emergency manager, witnessed the funnel cloud and verified that it never touched down.
Nickel sized hail was observed on the west side of Kemmerer near US Highway 30.
A peak wind gust of 66 mph was clocked at Dubois Municipal Airport.
The Elkhorn RAWS measured a wind gust to 62 mph.
Wind gusts at a rural subdivision west of Riverton were estimated at 65 mph for several minutes.
An 80 mph wind gust was measured at the Grass Creek Divide RAWS in the foothills of the southern Absaroka Range.
A backcountry traveler observed penny sized hail that accumulated to a depth of several inches near Union Peak.
Golf ball sized hail was observed near the Eastridge Mall and in Evansville.
One inch diameter hail was observed at a ranch in the shadow of Copper Mountain in northern Fremont County.
Numerous reports of 1.5 inch diameter hail came from east Casper.
Wind gusts of 60 to 71 mph were measured by an anemometer along Interstate 25 north of Casper.
Hail of nickel to quarter size fell in Casper.
The ASOS at the Rock Springs-Sweetwater County Airport registered a wind gust to 61 mph at 1336MST.

Two rounds of rain totaling one-half inch to one inch in less than one hour produced a series of mud and rock slides across US Highway 14/16/20 near the east gate of Yellowstone National Park. The largest slide was about 100 feet wide and ranged from three to six feet in depth. Several smaller slides along the highway were spread across an area one to two miles wide centered around milepost 7.5. Mud, rocks, logs, and other debris clogged one box culvert and covered the road within this stretch of highway. The road was closed for about eight hours as Wyoming Department of Transportation crews cleared the debris. The slides occurred during the height of the tourist season and the temporary road closure stranded hundreds of motorists on both sides of the blockage.
Hail up to the size of nickels fell at Pahaska.

Slow-moving thunderstorms produced very heavy rain near the Red Wall and Gray Wall in northern Natrona County. Radar estimated up to 3.5 inches of rain fell within one hour in the Hackett Creek drainage, while widespread 1.5 inch amounts were estimated across a larger area near the walls. The Alkali, Indian, and Willow creek drainages were significantly impacted.||Damage to county roads was extensive as culverts could not handle the volume of water and debris which washed down hillsides and across the roads. There were numerous instances of water, mud, and debris across Willow Creek and Baker Cabin roads. Small reservoirs quickly filled with water and overflow channels were utilized. Large hail also occurred with the thunderstorms which further complicated the situation. Hail stones larger than a quarter were still visible in deep drifts the morning after the deluge. Hay meadows, backcountry roads, and ranch fence line were all damaged by the flood waters and hail.||Near the Willow Creek Ranch and downstream near the rural Willow Creek School, the flood waters on Willow Creek were estimated at over 100 yards wide and at least 4 to 5 feet deep. The high water re-routed the creek and left a large amount of sediment and debris behind. Farther upstream near the two walls, the flood waters tore loose the soil and grass of Hackett Creek scouring out the creek bed. Numerous fences were destroyed and at least one residence reported flooding near the school. The school itself was damaged when a small drainage overflowed a county road sending water and debris cascading into the building.

Large hail fell along the western edge of a violent thunderstorm that produced widespread flash flooding. The hail was estimated to be 1.5 in diameter. The rain washed the hail into large piles and drifts within meadows at the western base of the Red Wall.

Heavy rain caused several mudslides across US Highway 89 around milepost 120 in the steep terrain of Snake River Canyon east of Alpine. Rainfall totals were estimated at one-half to three-quarters of an inch in less than 40 minutes. The highway was closed for about three hours and several vehicles were damaged. The slides, mostly composed of mud, were three to four feet deep in some places.
A sheriff's deputy observed and photographed a funnel cloud west of Marbleton around 1600MST.
The Poker Creek RAWS site registered a wind gust to 59 mph.
The SNOTEL at Shell Creek reported 16 inches of snow.
Heavy snow fell across the eastern Bighorn Range. The maximum was 20 inches at the Little Goose SNOTEL.
There were widespread reports of 7 to 10 inches of snow throughout Buffalo. The snow fell on trees with full foliage, resulting in many downed limbs and scattered power outages throughout Buffalo.
Hailstones up to ping pong ball size fell just north of Smoot.
A long-track thunderstorm produced penny sized hail in Thermopolis.
Trees 50 to 60 feet tall were toppled in the town of Jackson by outflow from a collapsing thunderstorm. At least one vehicle was damaged.

Rainfall of one-half to one inch fell in 20 to 30 minutes in the steep terrain of Paintbrush Canyon. A National Park Service backcountry trail crew working in the canyon reported hearing a rumbling sound before witnessing a large mudslide. The slide washed out multiple sections of the popular Paintbrush Canyon trail. The crew sought higher ground and all were safe, but the slide did destroy some gear and equipment.
Widespread 6-8 inch snowfall totals were observed in the Absaroka Range.
The ASOS at the Worland Municipal Airport clocked a 58 mph wind gust from the west at 1224MST as a thunderstorm rolled east across Washakie County.
The CWOP weather sensor 5 miles WNW of Clark recorded several wind gusts past 58 mph with a maximum wind gust of 83 mph at 1206MST.
The ASOS at Hunt Field in Lander reported a wind gust of 68 mph.

Outflow from a collapsing thunderstorm produced a 10-minute stretch of wind gusts from the west-southwest that exceeded 50 mph. The ASOS at Casper-Natrona County International Airport measured a peak speed of 64 mph at 1401MST.
Several wind gusts over 58 mph were recorded around Clark with a maximum wind gust of 61 mph.
Several wind gusts of over 58 mph were recorded in the vicinity of Clark. The maximum wind gust was 84 mph reported 5 miles WNW of Clark.
The official observer at the Lander Airport measured 8.1 inches of snow. Other measurements around Lander ranged from 6 to 8 inches.
Trained spotters reported from 8 to 10 inches of snow around Thermopolis.
The ASOS at the Greybull airport reported a wind gust to 66 mph with the passage of an Arctic front. The strong winds caused some power outages in the town of Greybull.

Temperatures at the Casper-Natrona County International Airport set three record low temperatures from Tuesday, November 11, until Thursday, November 13. The minimum readings were 19 below, 27 below, and 26 below zero, respectively. The low of 27 below zero on Wednesday, November 12, was the all-time record low for November. Record low maximums were also recorded with highs of only 6 above, 3 above, and 8 above zero on the same three days. Wind chill temperatures fell to as low 43 below zero at Hiland on the 12th.

The ASOS at the Big Piney Airport set new record low temperatures of 15 below zero on November 12, and 18 below zero on November 13. Record low maximums were also recorded from November 11, 12, and 13, as temperatures only climbed to 15, 11, and 10 above zero, respectively.

Record low temperatures of 11 below and 13 below zero were set at the Johnson County Airport in Buffalo airport on November 12 and 13. Record low maximums were also for four straight days from the 11th through the 14th with readings of 9, 7, 11, and 13, respectively.

A new record low temperature of 16 below zero was achieved at the South Big Horn County Airport near Greybull on Thursday, November 13. New record low maximum temperatures of 6, 10, 15, were recorded on November 12, 13, and 14, respectively.

Record lows of 12 below and 20 below zero were recorded at Lake Yellowstone on November 11th and 12th, respectively. Record low maximums were also recorded with highs of 8 on the 11th and 9 on the 12th.

New record low temperatures of 13 below and 18 below zero were observed at Hunt Field in Lander on November 12 and 13, respectively. Also, a record low maximum of 3 above zero was recorded on both days.

A record low temperature of 21 below zero was recorded in downtown Riverton on Thursday, November 13. New record low maximum temperatures of 9 above zero, 4 above zero, and zero were set on November 11, 12, and 13, respectively.

The Rock Springs-Sweetwater County Airport recorded record low temperatures of 4 below, 11 below, and 12 below zero on November 11, 12, and 13, respectively. Record low maximum temperatures of 9, 4, and 11, were also observed on the same three days.

The Worland Airport recorded new record low temperatures of 21 below and 28 below zero on November 12 and 13, respectively. Record low maximums of 3 above on the 12th and 5 above on the 13th were also observed.
Trained spotters reported 6 to 8 inches of new snow around Cody.
Trained spotters measured 22 inches of new snow at the top of the Jackson Hole Ski Resort. Other notable amounts included 23 inches at the Grand Targhee SNOTEL.

Heavy snow fell through the Jackson Valley. The highest amounts were in northern areas where Moran reported 20 inches and 18 inches at Moose. Around the city of Jackson. amounts were generally 8 to 12 inches.

Heavy snow fell across portions of the Star Valley. The highest amount was near Thayne where 13 inches fell. Other areas around the northern Star Valley had 6-8 inches of snow. Lesser amounts in the southern Star Valley.
High winds occurred across most of the Green and Rattlesnake Ranges. The highest wind gust was 84 mph at Camp Creek.
Several wind gusts past 58 mph were recorded on Outer Drive south of Casper, including a maximum gust of 76 mph. The also Casper Natrona County airport reported a gust of 58 mph at 1226MST.
High winds blew in the vicinity of Clark. The highest wind was at the sensor 5 miles west of Clark where a gust of 103 mph was recorded with many gusts past 58 mph.
The SNOTEL at Granite Creek estimated 18 inches of new snow. One top of the Jackson Hole Ski Resort 13 inches of new snow was measured.
There were numerous reports of over 6 inches of snow across the Jackson Valley. Some of the higher amounts included 9.7 inches near Wilson and 9 inches near Teton Village.
Snowfall totaled 8 inches at Bedford and 9 inches south of Smoot, both favored in northwest flow aloft.
At Commissary Ridge 18 inches of new snow was estimated. The Willow Creek and Spring Creek SNOTELS estimated 12 to 16 inches of new snow.
Many strong wind gusts past 60 mph were measured in the vicinity of Clark. The strongest wind gusts was 92 mph at a sensor west of the town.
Winds were sustained above 40 mph at several sites in eastern Sweetwater County. The maximum wind gust was 59 mph at Snow Springs Creek.
Winds were sustained between 40 and 45 mph for nearly 3 hours around Kemmerer.

Heavy snow fell across the Tetons. Numerous locations reported over a foot of snow with some areas seeing over 2 feet. Some of the higher totals included 28 inches at the Grand Targhee SNOTEL and 26 inches at the Jackson Hole Ski Resort.

Heavy snow fell across portions of the Star Valley. The heaviest snow fell in the northern Star Valley where amounts at Alpine were up to 15 inches. Lesser amounts fell farther south where the snow mixed with rain at times.
A trained spotter at the High Country Lodge measured 28 inches of new snow. SNOTEL stations around the western Bighorn range recorded between 1 to 2 feet of snow.
The SNOTEL at Cloud Peak Reservoir estimated 13 inches of new snow.
Heavy snow fell across the Salt and Wyoming ranges. The highest amount was 29 inches at the Spring Creek Divide SNOTEL. Many other locations had between 1 and 2 feet of new snow.
A trained spotter measured 15.8 inches of new snow at the Lamar Ranger Station.
Heavy snow fell across portions of the Absarokas. Some of the highest totals included 16 inches at the Evening Star SNOTEL and 13 inches at the Beartooth Lake SNOTEL.
Heavy snow fell through the Jackson Valley. Amounts ranged from 5 inches in Jackson to 9 inches in Moose.
Heavy snow fell in the northern Big Horn Basin. Some of the higher snowfall totals included 13 inches at Shell and 10 inches at Lovell.

Heavy snow fell in the southeastern Big Horn basin. The highest amounts were noted around Ten Sleep and the Upper Nowood Valley where 7 to 11 inches fell. Lesser amounts fell farther west Washakie County.
Heavy snow fell across the western slopes of the Wind River Range. Many areas picked up over 1 foot of new snow. The highest amount reported was 14 inches at the Gunsight Pass SNOTEL station.
The Two Ocean Plateau SNOTEL station estimated 12-15 inches of new snow.
Heavy snow fell across portions of Park County. The heaviest snow fell near Clark where 11 inches of snow was measured. Around the city of Cody, 7 to 9.5 inches fell.
Numerous wind gusts of hurricane force were recorded at the highway sensor along Chief Joseph Highway. The maximum recorded wind gust was 88 mph.
Gusts of 59 to 68 mph were recorded to the west of Clark.
The wind sensor at the North Fork of the Popo Agie recorded several wind gusts past 58 mph with a maximum of 75 mph.
The ASOS at the Hunt Field in Lander reported a wind gust to 63 mph.
Strong winds blew across portions of the Green and Rattlesnake ranges. The maximum wind gust of 68 mph was recorded at Camp Creek.
A 65 mph wind gust was recorded at the Twenty Mile Hill weather sensor. In addition, an anemometer near Hiland peaked at 60 mph, while a 58 mph wind gust was reported at the Casper Airport ASOS.
The Piney Creek weather sensor clocked a peak gust of 65 mph. The ASOS at the Johnson County Airport in Buffalo reported several wind gusts past 58 mph, including a maximum of 64 mph.
The observer at Casper airport measured 9.3 inches of snow. Other locations around Casper measured from 7 to 11 inches of snow.
Trained spotters measured 6 to 7 inches of snow in Jeffrey City and Sweetwater Station.
Snowfall in the vicinity of Lander generally ranged from 5 to 9 inches.
Heavy snow fell across portions of Hot Springs County. The highest amount was 9 miles NE of Thermopolis near Lucerne where 13 inches of snow was measured.
Snowfall amounts across the southeast Big Horn Basin ranged from 7 inches near Worland to 12 inches south of Ten Sleep in the Upper Nowood Valley.
Trained spotters reported 6 inches of snow in Cody. The highest amount in the area was report east of Cody where over 10 inches fell.
Many wind gusts past 58 mph were recorded at the weather sensor 5 miles WNW of Clark. The maximum wind gusts were 91 and 92 mph between 0330 and 0430MST.
The RAWS site at Camp Creek had a maximum wind gust of 69 mph.

Several sites in eastern Sweetwater County had wind gusts past 58 mph. The highest gust of 67 mph occurred at Snow Springs. The ASOS at Rock Springs-Sweetwater County Airport clocked a gust to 59 mph.
Snowfall totals across the Star Valley ranged from 10 inches at Thayne to 5 inches at Afton where the snow mixed with rain at times.
Heavy snow fell across the Salt and Wyoming ranges with many areas seeing over 1 foot of new snow. The highest amount was 26 inches at the Spring Creek Divide SNOTEL site.
Heavy snow fell in the Tetons. At the Jackson Hole Ski Resort, 15 inches fell on the summit. The highest amount was 16 inches the Grassy Lake SNOTEL.
Snow amounts across the Jackson Valley ranged from 8.3 inches at Moose to 2 inches in the town of Jackson.
Heavy snow fell across portions of Yellowstone National Park. The highest total was 19 inches at the Lewis Lake Divide SNOTEL.
The Wolverine SNOTEL estimated 12 inches of new snow.
Snowfall amounts across the Upper Green River Basin Foothills ranged from 5 to 8.5 inches. The highest amounts fell north and west of Daniel.
A wind gust to 69 mph was recorded at the Johnson County Airport in Buffalo.
Heavy snow fell throughout Hot Springs County. The heaviest amounts were near Thermopolis where totals were 12 to 16 inches.
Heavy snow fell in the eastern slopes of the Wind River Range. The highest amounts fell in Sinks Canyon State Park where snowfall of 14 to 20 inches was measured.
Heavy snow fell in portions of Casper nearest Casper Mountain. Snowfall in this area ranged from 7 to 11 inches. Lesser amounts of 4 to 6 inches fell in other portions of the Casper area.
Snowfall of 12 to 18 inches was measured on Casper Mountain.
In Lander, 7 to 10 inches of new snow fell across town.
The cooperative observer in Jeffrey City measured 6 inches of snow.

Trained spotters measured 5 inches of snow in Green River and Rock Springs. The snow combined with northeast wind of 30 to 40 mph with gusts as high as 51 mph to make for treacherous travel on Interstate 80 across Sweetwater County.
Heavy snow fell in the Jackson Valley. Some amounts included 12 inches in Moose and 9 inches in the city of Jackson.
Heavy snow fell across the northern Star Valley. Alpine had 12 inches of snow with 8 inches at Star Valley Ranch. Lesser amounts fell farther south where Afton only measured 2.5 inches of snow.

Heavy snow fell in portions of the Upper Green River Foothills. The heaviest amounts fell west of Daniel where 16 inches was measured. Around a foot of snow was measured around Bondurant. Lesser amounts were noted around Pinedale.
Low temperatures around Jeffrey City City were -33F to -37F. In addition, wind chill temperatures below -30F were recorded through the day on Tuesday, December 30, and the morning of December 31.
Low temperatures in Riverton ranged from -30F to -36F.
The cooperative observer near Lucerne recorded an overnight low of -38F on Wednesday morning, December 31. The same location had 20 inches of snow on the ground.
A mesonet sensor near Kemmerer registered a low temperature of -30F on Wednesday morning, December 31. In addition, wind chill temperatures as cold as -43F were recorded.
Low temperatures at Afton and Etna were -33F and -30F, respectively, on Wednesday morning, December 31.

The wind chill across Natrona County, including at the Casper-Natrona County International Airport, fell below -30F for much of Tuesday, December 30, and the morning of December 31. The coldest wind chills occurred the evening of December 30.
Wind chill readings of -30F to -35F occurred on Casper Mountain, primarily on Tuesday, December 30.

The cooperative observer at the Daniel Fish Hatchery had a low temperature of -48F on the morning of Wednesday, December 31. The observer also reported 18 inches of snow on the ground. Other very cold temperatures included -42F at Bondurant and -35F at Boulder.
The airport in Big Piney had a low temperature of -35F on Wednesday morning, December 31.
Wind chill readings at the Rock Springs-Sweetwater County Airport fell as low as -38F early Wednesday morning, December 31.

The ASOS at the Worland Municipal Airport had a low temperature of -31F on the morning of Wednesday, December 31. In addition, a cooperative observer near Big Trails in southeast Washakie County recorded an overnight low of -34F.
The SNOTELs at Sylvan Lake and Two Ocean Plateau recorded an estimated 19 inches of new snow.

Very heavy snow fell in portions of the Tetons. The highest amounts were recorded at the Grand Targhee and Grassy Lake SNOTEL stations. In addition, 33 inches of new snow was measured on top of the Jackson Hole Ski Resort.
Trained spotters reported heavy snow in much of the Jackson Valley. Nearly 10 inches of new snow fell at Moose and Jackson.

Heavy snow fell in portions of the Star Valley. The heaviest snow fell at Alpine where 16.5 inches of new snow was measured. Farther south, 6 inches of snow was measured at Afton where warmer air caused the snow to mix with rain at times.
Heavy snow fell in the Salt and Wyoming Ranges. The highest total was 21 inches at the Spring Creek Divide SNOTEL site.
A trained spotter measured 7 inches of new snow at Bondurant.
The SNOTEL station at Evening Star estimated 26 inches of new snow. The Wolverine SNOTEL had 19 inches.
The SNOTEL site at Shell Creek estimated 16 inches of new snow.
Wind gusts of 88 mph were reported at both the Fales Rock and Camp Creek RAWS stations.
High winds blew on the south side of Casper. The weather sensor at Outer Drive recorded many wind gusts past 58 mph with a maximum of 81 mph.
Very strong winds occurred in the vicinity of Clark. The wind sensor 5 miles west of Clark had several wind gusts above hurricane force, including a maximum of 113 mph.
A wind gust of 61 mph was recorded at the Dubois Elementary School.
The AWOS at the airport near Kemmerer recorded a wind gust of 60 mph.
Numerous wind gusts over 58 mph were recorded at the Snow Springs Creek RAWS including a maximum of 66 mph. The Rock Springs Airport ASOS had a wind gust of 59 mph at 0524MST and 1146MST.

A prolonged period of high winds occurred over the Cody Foothills. The strongest winds occurred in the vicinity of Clark, where there were numerous wind gusts over 74 mph with a maximum wind gust of 117 mph. In Cody, wind gusts to 82 mph caused scattered power outages and downed trees. One of the trees fell on the visitors center in downtown Cody on Sheridan Avenue.
Several wind gusts past 58 mph were recorded at a weather station near Clark. A peak gust of 75 mph was measured at 1718MST.
High wind gusts were found across the Green and Rattlesnake ranges. The highest wind gust was 82 mph at Camp Creek.
Strong wind gusts blew along Wyoming Boulevard on the south side of Casper. The highest wind gust was 75 mph. Winds were not as strong farther north.
A foot of new snow was measured on top of the Jackson Hole Ski Resort.

Winds gusted past 60 mph in the vicinity of Clark. The strongest winds occurred at the sensor 5 miles west-northwest of Clark where there were several wind gusts exceeded 74 mph with a maximum of 91 mph.
The higher elevations of the Green and Rattlesnake ranges saw high wind gusts. The highest wind gust was 76 mph at Fales Rock.
Strong winds blew on the south side of Casper. The weather sensor at Outer Drive had several wind gusts past 58 mph with a maximum gust of 71 mph.

The SNOTEL site at Phillips Bench estimated 20 inches of new snow. Heavy snow also fell at Grand Targhee where 18 inches fell. The higher elevations of the Jackson Hole Ski Resort also picked up over a foot of new snow.
Heavy snow fell in the Salt River and Wyoming ranges. The heaviest was at the Triple Peak SNOTEL where 17 inches of new snow was estimated.
The Piney Creek mesonet station recorded sustained winds of about 40 to 43 mph for approximately 2.5 hours.
The peak wind on Chief Joseph Pass was clocked at 86 mph.
Wind gusts to near 100 mph toppled power poles and caused power outages in rural areas around Meeteetse.
Strong winds occurred in portions of the Green and Rattlesnake ranges. The highest wind gust recorded was 82 mph at Fales Rock RAWS. Gusts to 65 mph were recorded at Beaver Rim and Camp Creek RAWS.
The wind sensor at Outer Drive near Casper had a wind gust to 72 mph. Other strong wind gusts included 62 mph at Hiland, and 59 mph at the Casper-Natrona County International Airport.
A 78 mph wind gust was recorded at Red Canyon.
A wind gust of 74 mph was recorded at a ranch along the North Fork of the Popo Agie River. The ASOS at the Lander Airport had a wind gust of 59 mph.
The weather sensor at Piney Creek had a wind gust of 65 mph. The ASOS at the Buffalo Airport had a wind gust to 58 mph.
The wind sensor on Interstate 25 north of Kaycee measured several wind gusts past 58 mph including a maximum of 68 mph.
A wind gust of 76 mph was recorded at Grass Creek Divide RAWS.
Dramatic video captured a snowmobiler caught in and eventually buried by an avalanche. Companions quickly came to his rescue and uncovered the man.
A mesonet sensor very near the town of Clark measured wind gusts of 63 and 59 mph during the late evening.
The SNOTEL site at Middle Powder River estimated 12 inches of new snow.
The observer at the Lander airport measured 7.7 inches of new snow.
Heavy snow fell south of Ten Sleep. New snow measurements varied from 8 to almost 14 inches.

Several wind gusts past 60 mph were recorded at the Johnson County Airport in Buffalo. The wind combined with a period of moderate to heavy snow that brought near whiteout conditions and led to several accidents and closures of interstates 25 and 90 for several hours.
Lander reported 6 inches of snow at 0500MST.
An NWS employee reported 6 inches at Sand Draw southeast of Riverton.
Snowfall of 6.2 inches was reported about 4 miles southwest of Casper.
Snowfall totals topped one foot on Casper Mountain.
A rural ranch in northeast Sweetwater County received about one foot of snow.
A peak wind gust to 81 mph was clocked west of Clark at 1619MST.
A sensor on Chief Joseph Pass registered a few wind gusts to 77 mph and there were extended periods of sustained winds over 50 mph.
Sustained wind of 50 to 55 mph was measured by a sensor on Chief Joseph Pass.
A trained spotter measured 14 inches of new snow 6 miles southwest of Lander near Sinks Canyon State Park.
A sensor on Chief Joseph Pass registered a wind gust to 94 mph.
Sustained hurricane force winds with several gusts in excess of 100 mph occurred west-northwest of Clark. The wind caused damage to at least one home.
A few wind gusts past 58 mph were reported at the Johnson County Airport in Buffalo, including a maximum gust of 60 mph.
A wind gust of 78 mph was reported at the wind sensor on the Chief Joseph Highway.
Strong wind gusts occurred in a few locations across the Cody Foothills. The highest gusts were near Clark including a maximum of 84 mph.

A mountain wave developed over the Wind River Range and brought high winds to the Lander foothills. The highest wind gust reported was 71 mph at the Lander airport. The wind tore the sheet metal off of an outbuilding in Lander.
The ASOS at the Casper/Natrona County International Airport had a wind gust to 63 mph.
The cooperative observer measured ten inches of snow at Powder River. Accumulations were less across the remainder of Natrona County, generally ranging from two to five inches.
The cooperative observer measured seven inches of snow at Jeffrey City.

The observer at the Lander Airport measured 7.6 inches of snow. Amounts around the Lander foothills generally ranged from 3 to 9 inches, with the higher amounts in the high elevations toward Sinks Canyon State Park.
The SNOTEL site at St. Lawrence recorded 18 inches of new snow. Other notable amounts included 16 inches at the Cold Springs SNOTEL and 13.5 inches at the University of Missouri Geology Camp.
Penny sized hail fell across a swath of I-25 between mileposts 262 and 267. The hail accumulated to a depth of several inches.
A wind sensor along I-25 near Reno Hill north of Kaycee registered wind gusts around 60 mph with a peak of 62 mph.

The peak wind at North Big Horn County Airport near Cowley was clocked at 59 mph at 1935MST. The AWOS at Powell Municipal Airport recorded sustained wind over 40 mph for more than an hour during the late evening.
A WYDOT mesonet sensor near Continental Divide on I-80 registered sustained wind over 40 mph for more than one hour late in the afternoon.
A cooperative weather observer measured six inches of snow at Jeffrey City.
Trained spotters measured 4 to 10.5 inches of snow around Casper. The highest amounts of snow were in south Casper, near the foothills of Casper Mountain.
Trained spotters measured anywhere from 16 to 22.5 inches of new snow on Casper Mountain.
A trained spotter reported nickel sized hail on the southwest shore of Lake DeSmet.
The public witnessed four funnel clouds south of US Highway 20/26 between Shoshoni and Moneta.
A trained spotter reported hail up to the size of nickels covering US Highway 14/16/20 near milepost 71.

A Bureau of Land Management law enforcement officer reported a rope tornado in eastern Park County. The tornado remained over open country and caused no damage. The twister was photographed from both the west and east sides.

Several storm spotters reported flash flooding on Salt Creek and Castle Creek in the vicinity of Midwest. Some county and Bureau of Land Management roads were washed out. At least one fracking trailer was destroyed south of town.
Trained spotters reported flood waters up to buildings on the south side of Bar Nunn.
Heavy rainfall of two to three inches fell across northern Johnson County and caused flooding along Clear Creek. The flooding was mainly over low lying fields and caused little to no damage.

Very heavy rain fell in southern Hot Springs County. This triggered numerous mud and rock slides, some tumbling several hundred feet or more to the bottom of the Wind River Canyon. State Highway 789 through the canyon was covered with mud, rock, and debris in several locations between mileposts 120 and 123. One Wyoming Department of Transportation employee was briefly trapped in his front-end loader as he tried to clear away small slides at the onset of the event. The massive amount of debris on the highway resulted in the closure of the road from Sunday afternoon, May 24, until Wednesday morning, May 27. Additional slides on the west side of the Wind River Canyon destroyed several sections of railroad track that resulted in a halt of train traffic for several days.

Heavy rain caused flooding near the town of Thermopolis. South of Thermopolis, Buffalo Creek overflowed its banks and flooded nearby low lying areas. A mobile home community experienced flooding in East Thermopolis as small creeks and streams were inundated with water.

Thunderstorm outflow wind descended the east slopes of the Teton Range and generated a swath of damage from near Wilson north along the Moose-Wilson Road and through Grand Teton National Park. The damage began near Wilson around 1645MST and spread north until shortly after 1700MST. Downed trees damaged power lines, crushed parked vehicles, made roads impassable, and even stranded park visitors on the Signal Mountain Summit Road. Just under 1000 customers were impacted by power outages due to the downed power lines, including park employee housing at Beaver Creek. In all, over 150 trees were cleared and all park visitors were rescued by 2200MST.
Yellowstone National Park dispatch indicated 50 trees down between Lake and Sylvan Pass near the East Entrance to the park.
Pea to nickel sized hail fell just west of Kirby.
There were several public reports of ping pong ball to golf ball sized hail from just west of Kaycee, through Kaycee, and east along State Highway 192.

Minor flooding of the Greybull River occurred just south of Greybull near State Highway 789. The flooding occurred at the confluence of the Greybull River and the rain-swollen Big Horn River.
